title: Food & Beverage Ecommerce Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Conversion rate, AOV and bounce rate benchmarks for the Food & Beverage ecommerce category in 2026.
body_markdown:
## High CVR, Steady AOV — and a Q3 Pullback Milder Than Usual


The benchmarks:[2.99% median CVR](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$174 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) (January–September 2026). The 25th–75th percentile AOV range is $109–$334. Food & Beverage ranks third in CVR across the 10 published industries, and its top quarter of stores converts above 6.30% — the highest P75 in the dataset.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Food & Beverage.


CVR fell 16.5% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters, giving back part of the category’s 22.6% Q2 surge. Context matters here: Q3 is seasonally soft for Food & Beverage. Over the same quarters in 2025, CVR fell 27.9%, so Q3 2026 came in 11.4 percentage points better than the prior-year pattern. Through the first half of the year, every month ran above its 2025 equivalent; Q3 broke that streak, with July and September coming in below their year-ago levels.


On order value: $174 is tied with Health & Wellness for the lowest median in the dataset. That reflects the nature of the category — frequent, smaller purchases rather than high-ticket items. AOV rose 6.7% from Q2 to Q3 among stores active in both quarters ($173 to $185), the third-largest Q3 gain of any category, while matched year-over-year AOV was flat (−0.1%). In Q3, basket size did more of the work than conversion.


> Food & Beverage gave back part of its Q2 conversion surge in Q3 — but less than it usually does. CVR fell 16.5% against a 27.9% drop over the same months last year, while same-store AOV rose 6.7%.


## **Conversion Rate Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The median Food & Beverage CVR from January through September 2026 was 2.99%, third among the 10 published industries.


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


The top three converting categories — Health & Wellness, Beauty & Personal Care, and Food & Beverage — share a pattern. Customers in these categories tend to know what they want before they arrive. They are buying something they have bought before, or something close to it. That familiarity may contribute to a faster session-to-order cycle, though the data alone can’t confirm the mechanism.


The P75 for Food & Beverage CVR is 6.30% — the highest upper tail in the dataset. Some stores in this category convert at rates that would be exceptional in any other industry. The wide spread likely reflects a mix of subscription-style merchants, DTC brands with highly loyal audiences, and one-off purchase stores.


> The 2.99% median sits well above the cross-industry median of 1.74%. But the P75 of 6.30% suggests there is a cohort of Food & Beverage merchants converting at rates the category headline doesn’t fully capture.


## **CVR & Bounce Rate Trend — January 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Food & Beverage stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network.


n=30–44 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Food & Beverage.


The 21-month data shows a category that strengthened through late 2025 and the first half of 2026, then cooled in Q3. From January through June 2026, every month came in above its year-ago equivalent, capped by June 2026 at 4.61% against 3.83% in June 2025. Q3 broke the streak: July (3.33%) and September (2.32%) came in below 2025, with only August (3.45%) above.


November 2025 stands out sharply at 5.18% — the highest single-month CVR in the 21-month window for this category. One possible explanation is that food and beverage purchases tend to increase around the holidays as people stock up, gift specialty items, or order for gatherings. But that’s a hypothesis; the data shows the spike without telling us why.


September 2026 is the outlier in the other direction. At 2.32%, it was the lowest monthly CVR in the window. Monthly figures rest on 30–44 stores, so a single month can swing on a handful of merchants — but it’s a reading worth watching into Q4.


Bounce rate tells the same Q3 story. Through 2025 and the first half of 2026, it held in a roughly 40%–50% range with no sustained trend. Q3 broke out of that range: 53.2% in August and 60.8% in September, the two highest readings in the window. Rising bounce alongside a September conversion dip points to a late-quarter shift in traffic quality or mix rather than a slow drift.


## **Average Order Value Benchmark — 2026 Year to Date**


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Food & Beverage was $174, tied with Health & Wellness for the lowest of the 11 categories we track. This data set covers full-store Shopify order data, separate from the CVR cohort above.


January–September 2026, n=305 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Food & Beverage.


## **AOV Trend — June 2025 through September 2026**


The chart below tracks monthly median AOV for Food & Beverage stores, with each month measured on its own (239–327 stores per month).


n=239–327 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Food & Beverage.


The AOV trend remains one of the flattest in the dataset. Apart from November 2025 ($191), every month in the 16-month window sits between $160 and $181. From January through August 2026, the range was tighter still — $166 to $177.


November 2025 ($191) is the clearest departure from that band. Whether that reflects gifting behavior, larger holiday orders, or something else in the mix is unclear from the data alone. What the data does show is that it was temporary — AOV returned to $172 in December.


September 2026 ($181) was the highest month outside of November, and above September 2025 ($174). It lines up with the same-store Q2→Q3 gain: basket sizes rose in Q3 even as conversion softened.


On a matched same-store basis (n=206 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV was flat at $179 — a −0.1% year-over-year change. In a category defined by small, frequent purchases, price points have held steady.


## **What CVR and AOV Are Saying Together**


Food & Beverage grew through conversion volume in the first half of 2026, not basket size. Q3 shifted that balance: conversion pulled back from its Q2 peak, while same-store AOV rose 6.7%. Year over year, basket sizes are flat (−0.1%) among stores active in both periods — consistent with a category where price points are set by the nature of the product, not by seasonal demand swings.


The combination of high CVR and low AOV is worth understanding on its own terms. Food & Beverage merchants win on frequency and conversion; categories like Sports & Outdoors or Autos & Vehicles win on ticket size. Benchmarking against the wrong category’s numbers will mislead in either direction.


Read together, the Q2 surge and the Q3 pullback are more useful than either alone. Six consecutive months beat the prior year through June; Q3 broke that run, but the category still finished the quarter well ahead of its usual seasonal decline. Whether September’s dip is a blip or the start of something is the question for Q4.


> If your Food & Beverage CVR is at or above 2.99%, you’re at the category median or better. If your AOV is well above $174, you may be in a sub-market — specialty, premium, or B2B food — where this benchmark understates your opportunity.


## **A Note on Sub-Markets Within Food & Beverage**


The $174 median and the $109–$334 P25-to-P75 range reflect a category that is more price-consistent than most. The 3.1× spread is narrower than categories like Beauty & Personal Care (4.2×) or Home & Garden (4.2×). Most Food & Beverage merchants in this dataset operate at relatively similar price points.


That said, the category spans a wide range of business types. A subscription coffee brand, a direct-to-consumer hot sauce company, and a specialty cheese retailer are all “Food & Beverage” — but they have different order structures, purchase frequencies, and customer relationships. The stores above the P75 ($334) may be capturing large wholesale or gifting orders that push AOV well above the typical transaction.


CVR is the more meaningful benchmark for this category than AOV. At nearly 3%, the median is strong by any standard — and the upper end of the distribution suggests that some stores in this category have built purchasing patterns that convert at rates rarely seen outside of subscription commerce.


> The $174 AOV benchmark is the right reference point for most Food & Beverage merchants. But the CVR benchmark — and whether you’re above or below 2.99% — is likely the more actionable number for diagnosing performance.
